body: Seeing this as well. For some reason, the Control's pristine field doesn't become false until the second change.
I'm having a hard time replicating this.  Is this still a problem in rc.1?   An example plunker would help.

This is still a problem, and I've just run into it on my app. I'm attempting to use `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` in all my components, so it might be related to that.

The easiest workaround I've found so far is to embed `{{form.valueChanges.mapTo(null) | async}}` somewhere in the template to force the view update after form has changed, instead of before.

Edit: I'm also using Angular 2.0.0-rc.1 and Ionic 2.0.0-beta.7. I've also tried to reproduce this minimally in a Plunker (with just Angular) to no avail. The problem is everywhere in my app, but the Plunker works flawlessly...

body:
Removing `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` makes the problem go away, and reinstating it brings the problem back. And each view update `form.dirty`, `form.pristine`, etc. are always set to what their values should have been _before_ the latest keypress.

Edit: I've traced the event flow all the way back to https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/a31e2f5f4799e9ce20ae508f9f91dfeba05805f2/modules/angular2/src/common/forms/directives/shared.ts#L33-L38 with no problems. The callback passed to `valueAccessor.registerOnChange()` is actually being called immediately with the new value, as expected. Typing a single character into a form control results in 2 value updates, 3 change detector checks and no view update. Every subsequent character results in a view update as well, but with the form model that should have been used in the previous update.

Going even deeper down the rabbit hole: heavy use of console logging in seemingly relevant places has led me to the actual order of events.

For each event for the inputs in my app, the following happens:

`view.markPathToRootAsCheckOnce()` from https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bb8976608db93b9ff90a71187608a4390cbd7a07/modules/%40angular/compiler/src/view_compiler/event_binder.ts#L78
`control.updateValue()` from https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0a872ffd387f59b18128dc31d7fa874766bc22af/modules/%40angular/common/src/forms/model.ts#L294
`valueAccessor.onChange()` from https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/bb8976608db93b9ff90a71187608a4390cbd7a07/modules/%40angular/common/src/forms/directives/shared.ts#L38

This sequence repeats once more, running a total of 2 times (identical values both times, is this doubling-up a bug?), followed by a single value being emitted from `form.valueChanges`.

There are no calls to `view.markPathToRootAsCheckOnce()` or `view.markAsCheckOnce()` after the form model/control group has finished updating. Triggering a call to `view.markPathToRootAsCheckOnce()` manually by moving focus or any other method immediately updates the view with the correct form data.
Can you please provide an example plunker?

issue.title: forms: using <formControl>.updateValue(item) doesn't set the control to dirty and markAsDirty() fails too
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...**  (check one with "x")

```
[X] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior**
Updating the value of a form control using the updateValue() method will set the value correctly, but the 'dirty', 'touched' and 'pristine' properties of the control do not update. using the .markAsDirty() method fails to work. This is also described in issue #5328 
Only when you physically interact with the control do the values/flags update. 

**Expected/desired behavior**
updateValue(...) should update the flags appropriately, or have some documented way to programmatically update the value/flag states in one go.

**Reproduction of the problem**
http://plnkr.co/edit/ue2vlkzQ6Co4vDhzk0t0?p=preview

**What is the expected behavior?**
FormControl's should be updated with the correct state. ie. if the value changes then the control is now 'dirty'

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
Unless there is a misunderstanding on the use of FormControl (that it represents the state of an 'input' element) then the updateValue() method should work predictably.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
- **Angular version:** 2.0.0-rc.4 | **Forms:** 0.2.0
- **Browser:** [Chrome 51.0.2704.106 ] 
- **Language:** [TypeScript 1.8.10]

body: @tijoforyou Okay, I think I see what you mean.  Are you checking the pristine property in a subscription to valueChanges?    If you print the property to the screen with {{ }}, the pristine property updates right away (which is what I checked before), but if you check as part of valueChanges, it won't be correct right away because the order of the calls.  I think we should be able to just invert them.  Looking into it.
This is still a problem in Angular 7
I face the same problem with Angular 7.  Anyone has got a solution?
